subject.title: feat: add jsonl support to memory indexer

question: Should builtin memorySearch.extraPaths support arbitrary raw JSONL logs, or should raw log search stay in QMD/session-memory/converter-plugin workflows?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but adding arbitrary JSONL expands sensitive raw-message indexing beyond today's Markdown/multimodal/session contracts and conflicts with the core-lean guardrail unless maintainers want this in builtin memory.

options.title: Document external workflow
options.body: Keep builtin extraPaths limited to Markdown/multimodal files and document QMD, session-memory, or converter-plugin ingestion for raw JSONL logs.

options.title: Add native JSONL support
options.body: Implement JSONL as a first-class builtin extraPaths format with security review, line mapping, memory_get support, watcher coverage, docs, and regression tests.

options.title: Extend plugin API first
options.body: Define a memory-ingestion plugin seam so structured log formats can live outside core without losing search integration.

recommendation.title: Document external workflow
recommendation.body: Keep builtin extraPaths limited to Markdown/multimodal files and document QMD, session-memory, or converter-plugin ingestion for raw JSONL logs.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete already provided the prior maintainer-side review framing the same product/security choice, and the memory host history also routes through Peter Steinberger-authored refactors.
